newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares end slightly lower on wary mood.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares end slightly lower on wary mood.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index inched to a lower close in cautious trading on Wednesday after Tuesday's plunge on the Hong Kong stock market, brokers said.
The B share index shed 0.24 points or 0.15 percent to end at 162.25 points as turnover fell to HK$48.4 million from Tuesday's HK$73.3 million.
B share investors continued to move to the sidelines with the approach of the April 30 deadline set for listed companies to make public their 1996 results, brokers said.
"The Hang Seng's fall on Tuesday to some extent worsened investor confidence in the Hong Kong dollar in the the B shares here are denominated," a trader with J&A Securities (HK) Ltd said.
"But the market is more concerned by B share firms annual results to be published this month," the trader said.
Only three out of the 44 Shenzhen-listed B share companies have to date published their 1996 annual reports.
"Investors will be increasingly wary about trading," an analyst with China Guotai Securities said, adding trading is likely to remain quiet over the next few sessions.
"B share performance in the near future will also depend on the A share market, which seems to have lost direction after strong rises in the past weeks," the J&A trader said.
Beverage producer Shenzhen Shenbao Industrial Co Ltd, which has a joint venture with Pepsi Co Inc, dipped HK$0.23 or 3.87 percent to HK$5.71 on volume of 16,900 shares, making it the sharpest loser.
Wafangdian Bearing was the most active issue, slipping HK$0.03 to HK$5.03 on trade of 1.67 million shares.

The A share index edged down 2.61 points or 0.57 percent to close at 457.15 points due to investor disappointment over 1996 results released by a handful of A share companies on Wednesday, brokers said.
Turnover was 9.6 billion yuan compared with 10.1 billion on Tuesday.
